children: , the flash-memory and data-center storage producer, jumped 2.4% to approximately $1,779.24 Wednesday as the AI boom kept memory stocks running hot. That surge pushed the company's market value toward $279 billion, with investors betting that tight NAND supply and relentless data-center storage demand can keep the rally alive.

The latest fiscal fourth-quarter results delivered the numbers behind that enthusiasm. Revenue surged 51% sequentially to $8.97 billion, while gross margin reached 84.6%. Data-center sales more than doubled to $2.98 billion, roughly one-third of total revenue. Management now expects first-quarter sales of $10.30 billion to $10.80 billion and a gross margin between 83% and 84.9%.

The $10.55 billion midpoint points to another 17.7% sequential revenue increase, but the valuation leaves little room for disappointment. Long-term agreements already cover about half of fiscal 2027 bit shipments and two-thirds of fiscal 2028 volume, giving Sandisk more visibility than a typical memory-cycle winner. The GF Score chart tells the same two-sided story: powerful growth and financial strength stand out, yet a 51 out of 100 overall scorealongside weak GF Value and Momentum readingsshows that the stock's fundamentals and price still demand careful scrutiny.

title: Sandisk Jumps as AI Contracts Attack NAND's Boom-Bust Cycle
